parts.note: a chess player who concedes defeat before mate formally gives up the game with this word

explanation.surface: Someone abandons their hobby of chess.
explanation.definitionFit: Conceding a lost chess game by tipping over your king is the formal surrender every player knows.

clue.text: Response of soldiers being introduced to battle

parts.note: RE, the Royal Engineers, are soldiers
action is fighting, battle

explanation.surface: How troops react when first thrown into combat.
explanation.walkthrough: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps.
explanation.definitionFit: A reply or answering move to a stimulus.

indicators.note: the ship rounds, goes around, the letter taken from the pier

parts.note: a steamer is a steamship

indicators.note: end of means the last letter of the word pier

explanation.surface: The fleet's lead vessel sails round the tip of a jetty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flag-ship' looks like one word but splits: 'Flag' is the definition, 'ship' gives STEAMER, which 'rounds' R, the end of 'pier'.
explanation.definitionFit: A long narrow pennant or ribbon flown from a mast is a kind of flag.

explanation.surface: Someone mocks the fans.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock someone is to make fun of them; ropes holding a tent or mast steady are also called by this word.

definitions.note: a noun in the surface, but read as the phrasal verb 'get together'

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters of the exclamation and the A are put into an odd new order

explanation.surface: An exclamation of surprise at an odd social gathering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bless me!' looks like an exclamation but is the anagram fodder for 'strange'; the definition reads as the verb 'get together', not the noun for a party.
explanation.definitionFit: To gather people into one place is to meet up, the verb behind a social get-together.

parts.note: saving graces are redeeming features, but read literally these people have no grace for saving money

explanation.surface: People with no redeeming qualities at all.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saving graces' means redeeming virtues, but here it is the virtue of saving cash.
explanation.definitionFit: Wastrels who fritter money away never put anything by.

indicators.note: in a mess means the letters of the word are jumbled up

explanation.surface: A nobleman finds himself in genuine trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in a mess' rearranges REAL; 'in a' belongs with the indicator in the surface but gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A British nobleman ranking above a viscount and below a marquess.

explanation.surface: Someone grins broadly, feeling backed by friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinning broadly is one sense; a building with joists or girders holding it up is the other.

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
level means even, flat

explanation.surface: A football side draws level with Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Football and cricket sides each have this many players.

clue.text: Sets out an increase in salary, we hear

indicators.note: we hear tells the solver that the phrase spoken out loud matches the answer

parts.note: a raise is a pay increase, so 'an increase in salary' is A RAISE

explanation.surface: A document lays out a proposed pay rise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we hear' signals that A RAISE spoken sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To arrange things in order for display is to lay or set them out.

explanation.surface: A dietary instruction about cutting down on iron.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits as DE-CREASE: to remove creases, which is what ironing does.
explanation.definitionFit: To diminish is to get smaller, and pressing clothes with an iron takes the folds out of them.

parts.note: pro means for, in favour of
positions are places

explanation.surface: Proposals offered in exchange for locations.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans or suggestions offered for consideration are proposals.

parts.note: taken as written
an ad, an advertisement, is publicity

explanation.surface: A vain man who loves being in the public eye.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition calls up Mr Toad of Toad Hall, the boastful hero of The Wind in the Willows; 'given' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A loathsome or swaggering person is called this creature, like the vain Mr Toad of children's fiction.

clue.text: Edgar out to get a degree

indicators.note: out signals that the letters of the name are put out of their usual order

explanation.surface: A man called Edgar sets off to earn a university qualification.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges the letters of EDGAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A grade is a step or level on a scale, as a degree is.

clue.text: Information has bearing on hereditary factor

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
E, east, is a compass bearing

explanation.surface: Data that relates to an inherited trait.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal for information ('get the gen'); a bearing is a compass point, here E. 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The unit of heredity passed from parent to child is carried on a chromosome.

indicators.note: turn tells us to turn the following word round

parts.note: taken as written
mas are mothers; 'mother's' read as plural mums

explanation.surface: Someone arrives with their mum's pet cats.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn up' looks like 'arrive', but 'Turn' reverses UP to PU. 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cougars or mountain lions are large wild cats of the Americas.

parts.note: a serving man sounds like a footman or butler, but in tennis the server makes this error when the ball misses the box

explanation.surface: A butler or waiter makes a slip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving man' suggests a servant, but it is a tennis player serving.
explanation.definitionFit: In tennis a serve that fails to land in the right court is called this.

parts.note: a bounder is both a cad and something that bounds or leaps; a wily leaper keeps ahead of rivals by a hop

explanation.surface: A question about how a cunning cad managed to stay ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bounder' is old British slang for a cad, but here it is literally one who bounds, so staying ahead is measured in leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Staying a step in front of rivals is the idiom for keeping an advantage.

clue.text: Famous actor needs projection to reach his audience

definitions.text: Famous actor needs projection to reach his audience

parts.words: Famous actor needs projection to reach his audience
parts.note: projection sounds like voice projection on stage, but means the cinema projector putting a screen idol before viewers

explanation.surface: A celebrated stage performer must project his voice to be heard.
explanation.walkthrough: 'projection' suggests a stage voice, but it is the projector in a cinema.
explanation.definitionFit: A screen celebrity reaches cinema-goers only when the reel is run through a projector.

indicators.note: during puts the reversed word within the word for break

parts.note: a rent is a tear or break

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read backwards

parts.note: to cite is to call, summon to court

explanation.surface: While on holiday, someone phones their mother.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mum' looks like mother but is the adjective meaning silent, as in 'keep mum'; 'up' turns the word for call round in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping quiet and saying little is being silent, as in 'keep mum'.

clue.text: The strain of the French Revolution

definitions.text: The strain of the French Revolution

parts.words: The strain of the French Revolution
parts.note: strain means a tune, so this is the song that marched with the revolutionaries of 1792

explanation.surface: The stress and tension suffered during the French Revolution.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strain' looks like stress but means a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: France's national anthem was written in 1792 and taken up by volunteers from the south during the Revolution.

clue.text: In trouble, is repeatedly after credit

indicators.note: after places the repeated word behind the abbreviation for credit

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

indicators.note: repeatedly means the word is is written twice

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone in financial difficulty keeps borrowing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An emergency or time of acute difficulty.

parts.note: for can mean because of, as in 'jump for joy'
the ego is a person's sense of self

explanation.surface: Someone quits out of vanity.
explanation.definitionFit: To give up or do without something is to renounce it.

parts.note: a game bird is one shot for sport, but here it means a piece in a board game that shares its name with a black crow-like bird

explanation.definitionFit: The castle piece in chess shares its name with a gregarious crow.
A condition or position of affairs is one sense; to declare or say formally is the other.

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Soldiers find little to loot after a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft had 'Warriors make' as the definition, but 'make' is a link word ('Warriors make [what is in] some...'); IMPI means warriors alone.
explanation.definitionFit: A Zulu or Bantu regiment of fighters is known by this word.

explanation.surface: A dog, or a bit of one.
explanation.definitionFit: To follow someone closely is to shadow them, and a dog wags the rear appendage that is its other sense.

clue.text: Risky transaction with a Greek character

parts.note: a bet is a wager, a risky transaction

explanation.surface: A gamble undertaken alongside a man from Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The second letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: He designed furniture, to another's design

indicators.note: to another's design means the letters of the word are reshaped to a new pattern

parts.note: taken as written, the S included

explanation.surface: A furniture maker worked from someone else's plans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'design' rearranges ANOTHERS, all eight letters, the S included.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Sheraton was an 18th-century English cabinet-maker whose style of chairs and sideboards bears his name.
To resolve a matter is to fix it, and to make one's home somewhere is to take up residence there.

parts.note: to notice something is to spot it
less means fewer

explanation.surface: Seeing fewer marks on a clean surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Something perfectly clean has no stain or mark at all.

clue.text: One is supposed to look better for eating it

definitions.text: One is supposed to look better for eating it

parts.words: One is supposed to look better for eating it
parts.note: look better means see better: the old tale says this orange vegetable improves eyesight

explanation.surface: A food that is meant to improve your appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'look better' suggests appearance, but the folklore is that this root vegetable helps you see in the dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Popular belief holds that the orange root vegetable sharpens night vision.
